title: UKPNP and Swiss Kashmir Commission Stage Protest Outside UN Geneva Over Azad Kashmir Crackdown
excerpt: Rights organizations submit urgent memorandum to UN Secretary-General António Guterres, demanding an independent OHCHR fact-finding mission and an immediate end to the communications siege in Azad Kashmir.

body.text: HIGH-PROFILE DEMONSTRATION AT PALAIS DES NATIONS

Representatives of the United Kashmir People's National Party (UKPNP) and the Swiss Kashmir Human Rights Commission (SKHRC) staged a high-profile demonstration outside the United Nations headquarters in Geneva, protesting against reported state violence and human rights abuses in Pakistan-administered Azad Kashmir[cite: 12].

The demonstration brought together members of the Kashmiri diaspora alongside Baloch and Pashtun rights activists[cite: 12]. Organizers officially submitted an urgent memorandum addressed to UN Secretary-General António Guterres, the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR), and the UN Security Council, calling for immediate global intervention to halt kinetic operations against civil rights movements in the region[cite: 12].

The Joint Awami Action Committee has conducted a peaceful movement for three years, consistently advocating for negotiations and democratic rights. It is tragic that while authorities speak of peace globally, they deploy direct gunfire against civilians in their own periphery[cite: 12].
KEY ISSUES HIGHLIGHTED IN THE UN MEMORANDUM

During the rally outside the Palais des Nations, speakers led by UKPNP Chairman Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri outlined severe concerns regarding security deployments and administrative blockades in Poonch, Kotli, and surrounding districts[cite: 12]:

items: Civilian Fatalities Under Fire: Allegations that external paramilitary formations opened live fire on unarmed public gatherings, resulting in over 24 verified civilian deaths across Rawalakot, Kotli, and neighboring areas[cite: 12].

Proscription of Civic Movement: The use of the Anti-Terrorism Act (ATA) of 2014 to declare the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC)—a broad movement advocating for fair electricity tariffs and subsidized wheat flour—a 'terrorist organization' to justify security operations[cite: 12].

Collective Punishment and Blackouts: A complete suspension of cellular networks, broadband internet, and local press access, combined with road blockades that rights groups claim have created artificial shortages of food, fuel, and medical supplies[cite: 12].

Medical Facilities Affected: Reports that security personnel occupied local triage centers and medical hubs, obstructing wounded demonstrators, pregnant women, and elderly citizens from receiving critical care[cite: 12].

body.text: DEMANDS SUBMITTED TO THE UNITED NATIONS
The memorandum officially calls upon the United Nations and its affiliated human rights mechanisms to execute the following steps[cite: 12]:

items: OHCHR Fact-Finding Mission: Deploy an independent, international fact-finding mission to investigate massacres, unlawful killings, and allegations of enforced disappearances in Rawalakot and Kotli[cite: 12].
Withdrawal of Paramilitary Troops: Order the immediate withdrawal of heavy external paramilitary units from civilian population centers and healthcare facilities[cite: 12].
Restoration of Telecommunications: Force the immediate lifting of all digital and communication blackouts across Azad Kashmir[cite: 12].
Decriminalization of Dissent: Rescind the anti-terror notification proscribing the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) and release all arbitrarily detained activists[cite: 12].

Addressing the gathering in Geneva, UKPNP Chairman Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri emphasized that basic rights to life, assembly, and free expression cannot be subordinated to security measures[cite: 12]. The UKPNP reiterated that lasting regional stability depends on democratic engagement and strict adherence to international law covenants[cite: 12].
